title: P1: Add circuit breaker for LLM evaluator consecutive failures
description:
The _consecutiveLlmEvalFailures counter in AgentBackgroundService resets to 0 after hitting 3, creating an infinite detection-to-reset loop: fail→fail→fail→log ERROR→reset→repeat. No cooldown, no circuit-breaker, no exponential backoff. Each full cycle burns 3+ LLM calls before repeating the error message.

The counter provides no shielding against sustained failure. After N consecutive failures, the evaluator should be disabled for a cooldown period (e.g., 60s) or fall back to a deterministic "replan on any failure" rule.

Source: internal-audit-57-20260701.md — P1-9 [PR]

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body:
Sprint 59 Wave B: Completed remaining work on circuit breaker cooldown:

1. Changed LlmEvalCooldown from 5 minutes → 60 seconds (handoff spec)
2. Added pre-call guard in DispatchActionsAsync: skips evaluator when `_timeProvider.UtcNow < _llmEvalSuppressUntil`
3. Added pre-call guard in TryLlmReplanOnStallAsync: returns early during cooldown, letting governor's deterministic backoff handle the stall
4. Fixed log message from {CooldownMin}m → {CooldownSec}s

Previously the circuit breaker tracked failures and logged suppression but never actually prevented evaluator calls during cooldown — the infinite fail→log→call→fail loop continued unabated.

Build: 0 warnings, 0 errors. Tests: 815/815 passed.
